item_name: Receiver or add-on receiver migration routes
question_answered: When the original KeeLoq provisioning domain cannot be identified or supported, what authorized receiver-replacement or add-on-receiver routes can restore service, what do their credentials mean, what high-level installation facts must be verified, how are existing remotes affected, and how can the change be rolled back?
applicability_to_t5502_hcs301: Direct as a fallback for an owned Hiland T5502 installation when an additional T5502/HCS301 credential cannot be sourced or enrolled. Migration does not reproduce the T5502 secret or seed: it adds or substitutes a receiver with its own documented transmitter family. Exact applicability is conditional on the unidentified gate/door controller having a supported low-voltage activation input, suitable power, adequate enclosure/environmental provisions, and no proprietary or monitored input requirement [uncertain].
authorization_assumption: The requester owns the controlled premises and operator or has explicit written authority from the owner/administrator to alter its access-control wiring, credential population, and configuration. Shared, leased, workplace, strata/HOA, life-safety, and commercial systems require the responsible administrator and, where applicable, a licensed or qualified installer.
key_findings: Fact (manufacturer): purpose-built conversion kits exist that add a new rolling-code receiver to an older garage-door operator; Genie's GIRUD-1T documentation requires power isolation, connection to the operator's wall-button/common interface, wiring clear of moving parts, and disconnection of an existing external receiver.

Fact (manufacturer): commercial add-on receivers may expose one or more normally-open/common relay outputs and have explicit per-channel credential capacity. LiftMaster's 850LM, for example, has three N/O-COM relay outputs and stated channel capacities, but it uses LiftMaster credentials rather than Hiland T5502 credentials.

Fact (manufacturer manual): the Hiland R510X family accepts 12-24 VAC/DC, provides a relay rated 1 A at 30 VDC, has model-dependent rolling-code memory, and warns to power off before connection and not learn while the motor is operating.

Engineering inference: an isolated dry-contact relay can often emulate an approved momentary push-button input, but only the exact operator manual can establish the correct input, contact behavior, pulse duration, electrical isolation, power source, and whether monitored/proprietary signaling makes a generic receiver unsuitable.

Credential semantics: remotes enrolled to the add-on receiver are new credentials in that receiver's ecosystem. They are not cryptographic clones of the T5502 and ordinarily cannot operate the legacy receiver unless separately compatible and enrolled.

Existing-remotes impact: leaving the legacy receiver connected in parallel can preserve old remotes but also preserves every unrevoked legacy credential and expands the attack/maintenance surface. Disconnecting or removing it revokes legacy-radio access at once but makes old T5502 remotes stop operating that entry point.

Full receiver/controller replacement is appropriate where the radio is integral, inputs are proprietary, the old operator lacks current safety provisions, or the installation cannot be made compliant. It has the highest cost and requires recommissioning safety, limits, and all credentials.

Migration should not bypass photoeyes, sensing edges, emergency stop, manual release, fire/egress logic, or other entrapment protection. UL identifies UL 325 as covering operators and associated systems, while DASMA recommends qualified installation and testing all features before service.
primary_sources: Microchip Technology, 'HCS301 KEELOQ Code Hopping Encoder,' DS21143C, June 2011, https://ww1.microchip.com/downloads/en/devicedoc/21143c.pdf (accessed 2026-10-01).
Zhejiang Hiland Technology, 'R510X 1-channel receiver user manual,' Version A7, https://www.hiland.cc/system/storage/download/556/Receiver%20R5104%20user%20manual%20V7%20A7.pdf (accessed 2026-10-01).

The Genie Company, 'GIRUD-1T Universal Receiver Conversion Kit Installation Instructions,' https://store.geniecompany.com/pages/girud-1t-universal-receiver-conversion-kit-installation-instructions (accessed 2026-10-01).

FAAC, 'FSW900 Gate Operator Installation Manual,' manufacturer manual mirrored at https://www.faacgateopeners.com/FAAC-Manuals/FAAC-FSW900-Gate-operator.pdf (accessed 2026-10-01); it documents a generic receiver's N.O./common activation and 24 VDC power interface.

UL Standards & Engagement, 'UL 325: Door, Drapery, Gate, Louver, and Window Operators and Systems,' Edition 7, https://www.shopulstandards.com/ProductDetail.aspx?UniqueKey=32852 (accessed 2026-10-01).
secondary_sources: Door & Access Systems Manufacturers Association, 'Automatic Vehicular Gate Operating Systems,' TDS 352, https://www.dasma.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/01/TDS352.pdf (accessed 2026-10-01). Industry-association checklist; useful for commissioning practice but not a substitute for the operator manual or local code.

Door & Access Systems Manufacturers Association, 'Gate Openers: Safety Tips,' https://www.dasma.com/gate-openers/ (accessed 2026-10-01). Industry safety guidance recommending listed equipment, safe control location, demonstration, and periodic testing.

Reids Remotes, 'Hiland T5502 - 3 button black rolling code remote control,' https://www.reidsremotes.com.au/home/2748-hiland-t5502-3-button-black-rolling-code-remote-control.html (accessed 2026-10-01). Dealer evidence for legacy compatibility claims only; not sufficient to choose a migration receiver.
evidence_quality: High for the existence and general topology of manufacturer-supported add-on receivers, stated relay interfaces, capacity examples, and installation warnings because these come from manufacturer documentation. High for generic HCS301 learning/credential architecture. Moderate for applying any one example receiver to the requester's installation: the controller, radio module, input circuit, safety classification, environment, and jurisdiction are unknown. The FAAC source is a manufacturer manual hosted by a dealer mirror; its provenance is stronger than ordinary dealer advice but its applicability is model-specific. No source establishes that a generic add-on receiver is compatible with the unknown target operator.
source_dates: Microchip HCS301 DS21143C: June 2011. Hiland R510X manual: Version A7; publication date not printed in the retrieved text [uncertain]. LiftMaster 850LM and Genie GIRUD pages were current when accessed 2026-10-01; product revision dates were not stated [uncertain]. UL 325 Edition 7 was published 2017-05-19 and the indexed page reports revision through 2025-09-15. DASMA TDS 352 is dated/revised through 2023 in the retrieved document.
source_claim_type: Receiver voltage, contacts, memory, modes, learning, and warnings: manufacturer documentation.
Conversion-kit wiring topology and legacy external-receiver disconnection: manufacturer installation instructions.
UL 325 scope and revision status: standards-body page.
Commissioning and maintenance practices: industry-association guidance.
Parallel-versus-cutover effects and suitability of a dry contact for an unidentified controller: engineering inference requiring manual/installer confirmation.
relevant_components: Legacy T5502 transmitter and any legacy radio receiver/module; candidate add-on receiver and its matching genuine remotes; gate/door operator control board; documented low-voltage command input; isolated N.O./COM relay contacts; approved Class 2 or SELV power source where required; antenna and approved cable; enclosure, glands, strain relief, grounding/bonding as applicable; entrapment sensors, safety edge, emergency stop, manual release, fire/egress inputs, limits, and operator firmware. A full migration may also include a new operator/controller and fresh credential inventory.
hardware_revision_and_markings: Before selection, record the operator, controller, and radio-module maker/model, serial, manufacture date, PCB/revision, firmware, supply rating, input-terminal names, existing wiring, safety-device terminals, enclosure rating, and regulatory/listing marks. Record the candidate receiver SKU/revision, supported remotes, supply range, relay rating/type, duty mode, temperature/IP rating, antenna requirements, approvals, and memory capacity. The requester's exact receiver/controller markings are unknown [uncertain].
power_variant: The T5502 battery variant does not determine add-on-receiver power. Hiland R510X documents 12-24 VAC/DC, while other receivers may require a listed plug-in transformer or a specific regulated DC source. Never assume an operator's accessory terminal can supply the candidate load; verify voltage type, range, available current, polarity, commoning/isolation, fusing, and standby/battery-backup behavior from both manuals. Exact site power is unknown [uncertain].
rf_profile: A migration receiver may use a completely different certified radio protocol/frequency from the 433.92 MHz T5502 because its relay output bridges to the operator electrically. Compatibility is then between new remotes and the new receiver, not between T5502 and the new receiver. Select a region-approved product and manufacturer-supported antennas; receive-only checks may assess interference and coverage, but do not alter RF hardware or replay payloads.
observable_data: Without exposing secrets, document the legacy and candidate model labels, terminals, supply readings made by a qualified person, button/channel mapping, relay activation indication, antenna location, current inventory of working remotes, normal range, and operator response. A supervised continuity/voltage check on a de-energized or safely isolated control interface can establish whether an input is plausibly dry-contact, but the manual remains authoritative. Preserve before/after photographs, configuration exports where supported, serial numbers, and test results.
protected_or_secret_data: Legacy HCS301 crypt keys, secure-learning seed, synchronization state, receiver manufacturer code, and new-system administrative credentials are security-sensitive. Migration avoids needing the legacy secrets. Keep enrollment controls, backup memory, installer PINs, credential lists, and serial-to-holder mappings access-controlled; this report gives no secret values or recovery methods.
manufacturer_key_domain_evidence: A new receiver/remotes kit establishes its own documented vendor domain; evidence should be the receiver manufacturer's compatibility table, exact approved remote SKU, regional variant, manual, and traceable purchase. It need not share the Hiland manufacturer-key domain. If the plan instead expects T5502 remotes to work on the add-on receiver, obtain explicit Hiland/receiver-vendor confirmation naming both models; '433.92 MHz,' 'KeeLoq,' or 'HCS301' alone is insufficient.
compatibility_constraints: Operator-side: documented input type, pulse/latch semantics, voltage/current/isolation, channel mapping, safety logic, input priority, monitored/proprietary signaling, environmental rating, cable routing, power budget, standby behavior, and local/listing requirements. Radio-side: approved frequency/region, new receiver protocol and matching remote SKUs, antenna, capacity, interference, and firmware. Operational: whether old and new receivers may coexist, revocation policy, emergency/egress behavior, and availability of a qualified installer.
variant_conflicts: Products called 'universal receiver' are not universally interchangeable: LiftMaster 850LM is limited to specified code formats, Genie describes compatibility with garage-door interfaces under its instructions, and Hiland R510X has model-dependent rolling/fixed/open-code capacities and modes. Relay ratings and power ranges also differ. Resolve conflicts only from the exact product and operator manuals plus vendor written confirmation; do not infer suitability from a relay terminal or marketing word 'universal.'
access_assumption: No receiver-enclosure access prevents local wiring changes, so migration requires later authorized physical installation. No administrative access prevents lawful credential enrollment even if wiring is reachable. No RF reach prevents enrollment/range acceptance at the site. No participation by the legacy receiver does not block an independently wired add-on receiver, but the operator/controller must participate electrically and the installer must have authorized access. Full replacement requires broader mechanical/electrical access.
receiver_dependency: An add-on route does not depend on decrypting or reprogramming the legacy receiver; it depends on the new receiver learning its own remotes and its relay being accepted by the operator's documented command input. Parallel operation retains dependency on both radios for their respective remotes. Cutover disconnects the old receiver. Full operator/controller replacement removes the old radio/control dependency but requires complete recommissioning.
receiver_make_model_firmware: Unknown for the target [uncertain]. Establish from owner records, invoices, exterior labels, approved service menus, or a qualified installer's inspection. Do not assume the motor brand identifies an internal or third-party radio module. Obtain the exact manual revision and identify whether the activation input is conventional dry-contact, powered, bus-based, encrypted, monitored, or otherwise proprietary.
physical_access_vs_receiver_participatio: Planning and procurement can occur without enclosure access. Installing an add-on receiver or replacing the radio/controller requires authorized physical access, de-energization, safe wiring, and later powered commissioning. The legacy receiver need not participate if the new receiver connects independently to an approved operator input. The operator/controller and new receiver necessarily participate in operation and acceptance testing.
existing_authorized_remote_required: No for a fresh add-on or replacement receiver ecosystem, although one working legacy remote is useful for baseline comparison and rollback verification. Required only if preserving or testing a documented legacy enrollment path.
enrollment_method_and_authority: Enroll new, unique remotes only through the new receiver's documented local or administrative procedure after installation, under owner/administrator control. An installer should record which person holds each credential and each channel's purpose. Avoid open-code or permissive compatibility modes unless the risk owner explicitly accepts their documented lower security and the vendor supports the configuration.
credential_semantics: Add-on receiver: new unique credentials enrolled in a separate vendor domain. Replacement radio module: new credentials unless the manufacturer provides a supported migration/backup mechanism. Full controller/operator replacement: a new access-control domain. Parallel legacy/new operation is federation of two independent credential populations, not cloning. A receiver memory copy is legitimate only when the vendor documents it for owned systems; it is not proof of T5502 cryptographic duplication.
receiver_memory_and_revocation: Capacity and deletion behavior are product-specific. Inventory every old and new remote before change; determine per-credential delete, channel-specific erase, erase-all, backup/restore, full-memory behavior, and audit capability. Parallel operation requires governance of both memories. If the old receiver lacks individual revocation, disconnecting it may be the only reliable way to revoke lost legacy remotes. Never invoke erase-all without every authorized credential and a tested recovery plan.
legitimate_routes: Install a manufacturer-supported external conversion kit on a documented momentary control input and issue its matching rolling-code remotes.
Install a professional multi-channel dry-contact receiver where the operator manual explicitly permits that interface; map only the required channels.
Replace a plug-in or modular radio with an OEM-approved successor kit and enroll new approved remotes.
Temporarily run legacy and new receivers in parallel during a controlled credential transition, then disconnect the legacy receiver after all users migrate and revocation requirements are met.
Perform an immediate cutover by disconnecting the legacy external radio and enabling only the new receiver, accepting that old remotes cease to work.
Replace the controller/operator and radio as a complete listed/supported system when the radio is integral, the input is proprietary, or safety/lifecycle deficiencies make an add-on inappropriate.
prerequisites: Written authorization; exact operator/controller/radio identification; both manuals; verified input and power specifications; regional radio approval; compatible new receiver/remotes; credential inventory; documented safety devices and manual release; safe work-area control; rollback wiring/configuration record; and a qualified installer where mains, gate machinery, listed-system alterations, fire/egress, shared access, or local code are involved.
equipment_or_service_needed: Traceable genuine receiver/remotes, manufacturer-approved power supply/antenna/enclosure/accessories, normal insulated electrical test equipment used by a qualified installer, camera and labels for documentation, and operator-specific commissioning tools if authorized. A gate/access-control technician or garage-door professional should handle unfamiliar, mains-powered, monitored, commercial, or safety-critical systems. No cryptographic extraction or RF attack tooling is needed.
expected_outcomes: A successful add-on produces a separately managed credential set that activates only the intended operator input. A parallel transition preserves working old remotes until cutover; a disconnected legacy receiver makes them inactive at that entry point. OEM module or full-system replacement yields a supported current ecosystem. None of these outcomes reproduces the old T5502 identity, key, seed, or counter.
limitations: A relay interface cannot be assumed, may not preserve status/obstruction logic, and may be prohibited on proprietary or monitored inputs. Add-ons do not cure mechanical, entrapment, grounding, egress, fire, or obsolete-operator deficiencies. Parallel operation retains legacy credential risks. A new radio may have different range, latency, channel semantics, battery life, environmental limits, regional approval, and warranty/listing implications. Target-specific feasibility remains unknown until inspection [uncertain].
cost_or_effort_band: Supported external conversion kit: low to medium. Professional multi-channel receiver and documented wiring: medium. OEM radio-module replacement: medium. Parallel staged migration: medium operational effort. Full controller/operator replacement and safety remediation: high. Site, jurisdiction, trenching/cabling, enclosure, and labor costs are unknown [uncertain].
route_classification: Receiver migration and interoperability through an operator control interface; OEM radio replacement where available; credential re-enrollment in a new domain. It is not unsupported cryptographic duplication.
product_status_and_authenticity: Prefer a currently supported, region-approved receiver and exact matching remotes purchased from the manufacturer or an authorized dealer. Verify listing/certification marks, model/revision, serial/lot, packaging, firmware-support policy, warranty, return terms, environmental rating, and availability of replacement remotes. Marketplace 'universal KeeLoq' boards may have undocumented key domains, insecure open-code modes, counterfeit parts, no compliance evidence, and poor lifecycle support. Availability of any exact product in the requester's region is [uncertain].
feasibility_without_receiver: Without physical access to the legacy receiver but with authorized access to a documented operator input, an independent add-on receiver can be feasible because it need not use the legacy receiver. Without access to either the legacy receiver or the operator/controller wiring, migration cannot be installed. Without any participation by the legacy receiver, the new route remains feasible after proper installation; without participation by the operator/controller, no radio can actuate the system. Procurement alone is feasible off-site, but commissioning is not.
confidence: High that receiver migration is a legitimate alternative to secret duplication and that manufacturer-supported external-receiver kits use a new credential domain and control interface. High that existing-remotes behavior depends on retaining versus disconnecting their receiver. Moderate-to-low for the target's actual add-on feasibility because its operator, interface, safety configuration, site power, and jurisdiction are unknown.
legal_or_authorization_notes: Access-control alteration can affect property rights, tenancy/HOA rules, employment policy, insurance, fire/egress requirements, electrical/building codes, installer licensing, and product listing. Radio products must be lawful for the local region. Written owner/administrator authorization and local professional advice are appropriate for shared or commercial premises; legal counsel or the authority having jurisdiction should resolve disputed authority or life-safety/code questions.
operational_risks: Mains shock; short circuit or control-board damage; accidental gate/door motion; entrapment; defeat of safety, fire, or egress logic; incorrect latching versus pulse behavior; unintended channel action; reduced range or interference; power-budget overload; loss of battery backup; water ingress; credential lockout; preserving a lost legacy remote through parallel operation; memory erasure; and loss of evidence or baseline configuration. A moving gate can cause serious injury or death.
enrollment_side_effects: New enrollment consumes memory in the new receiver and may overwrite or reject credentials when full according to its manual. Erase-all can lock out every new user. Parallel operation leaves old credentials valid and can create duplicate commands. Cutover invalidates all legacy remotes at that entry point. Full replacement can change channel mapping, relay timing, range, audit behavior, and emergency/standby operation. Secure the area so no unrelated transmitter is learned during enrollment.
prohibited_actionable_details_omitted: Yes. No key or seed extraction, manufacturer-key recovery, cryptographic attack, rolling-code defeat, replay, brute force, protected-memory access, or unauthorized-entry instructions are included.
stop_conditions: Stop if authorization, operator identity, input semantics, power budget, wiring, safety-device status, fire/egress impact, local approval, or receiver authenticity is unclear; if wiring differs from the exact manual; if the gate/door moves unexpectedly; if any entrapment device, emergency stop, manual release, existing remote, or standby function fails; if memory behavior is unknown; or if a product requires bypassing a safety circuit. Escalate to the OEM, authorized dealer, qualified gate/garage-door/access-control installer, electrician, fire/life-safety professional, authority having jurisdiction, or lawyer as appropriate.
recommended_next_steps: Build a non-secret site dossier: operator/controller/radio labels, manuals, supply and input ratings, safety devices, old-remote inventory, normal behavior, and photographs of current wiring by an authorized person.
Ask the operator OEM or qualified installer whether an approved external receiver, OEM successor radio, or complete replacement is supported; obtain exact SKUs and written interface confirmation.
Choose a current, region-approved receiver with unique credential enrollment, individual revocation, adequate capacity, documented relay/power/environmental ratings, and traceable support.
Decide explicitly between parallel transition and immediate cutover, documenting when and how the legacy receiver will be disabled and lost credentials revoked.
Have a qualified installer de-energize, install, label, enroll one test credential, and execute a supervised acceptance test before enrolling the full population.
Retain before-state records and removed hardware securely until acceptance; then inventory credentials, document maintenance, and dispose of batteries/electronics appropriately.
questions_for_owner_or_vendor: What are the exact operator, controller, radio-module, firmware, manufacture date, and listing/certification marks?
Which terminal is the manufacturer-approved external activation input, and is it dry-contact, powered, bus-based, encrypted, or monitored?
What pulse/latch behavior and relay rating are permitted, and can the accessory supply safely power the receiver including standby operation?
Does adding an external receiver affect UL/CE or other listing, warranty, fire/egress behavior, or required entrapment protection?
Can the legacy and new receivers operate in parallel, and what exact action fully revokes legacy remotes at cutover?
What are the new receiver's per-channel capacity, full-memory behavior, individual-delete, erase-all, backup, audit, and firmware-support policies?
Are the receiver and remotes genuine, region-approved, currently supported, warranted, and returnable if compatibility testing fails?
rollback_and_acceptance_test: Before work, export or photograph configuration, label every conductor, record terminal voltages only through qualified procedures, inventory and test each existing remote/channel, verify manual release and every safety device, and preserve the old receiver unchanged. Use a reversible mounting/wiring plan and enroll only one new test remote. With an observer, exclusion zone, and emergency stop/manual release ready, verify de-energized wiring, power-up without motion, intended button/channel and momentary behavior, no unintended commands, safe normal-range operation, all photoeyes/edges/obstruction responses, stop/reverse behavior per the operator manual, emergency/egress and standby-power behavior, and every legacy remote expected to remain. Pass only if all functions match the documented baseline and safety manual. On any failure, de-energize and restore the labeled original wiring/configuration and old receiver; do not use erase-all. Re-test the complete original system before return to service and retain the failed receiver/records for vendor review.
